content.comment_body: Hello everyone, I have some experience with PLC programming from courses, but I am new to applying it. My question is quite basic: My [product_name] power supply has two '+' and two '-' terminals. I need to power my [product_name] base module and two [product_name] expansion modules, along with several buttons and other devices. I use 1.5 mm² wiring, but because of the wire end sleeves, I can only fit one wire in each contact. How is this usually managed? For buttons, I can use a ladder configuration with a common '+' wire, but with expansion modules, only one wire fits each terminal, so I can't easily daisy-chain them. Should I use a thinner wire? Also, my analog output module features two L+ and two M terminals that appear to be internally connected. Why are there two connections for each? Sorry if these are basic questions—I'm just starting out. Thanks in advance!

Welcome to the forum. In practice, bridged terminal blocks are typically used to distribute +24V and M (or L and N) from the power supply to each module. For analog modules, the power terminals are duplicated, meaning connections with the same name (like M) are internally bridged.
Thank you for your quick reply! I've ordered some terminal blocks with bridge connectors that should fit in the front, and I'm progressing step by step.
All [product_name] wiring supports max 2x 1.5 mm² or 1x 2.5 mm² cables. It is recommended to use ferrules. Make sure to review the manual.
For beginners, note that 'twin' ferrules are available for two 1.5mm² wires, which are easier to fit than using single ferrules on each wire.

analysis.insight_summary: People starting to wire [company_name] automation modules often run into problems with physical installation, such as distributing power among multiple modules with limited terminal space. There is also uncertainty about the purpose of duplicate terminals on analog modules. The discussion shows a need for practical advice and beginner-friendly wiring strategies.
analysis.user_expectations: Users seek clear, documented procedures for connecting multiple modules and devices, and explanations for why some modules have duplicate terminals.
